story: On Magnolia Loop, Gary is reading the street bulletin board for Architectural Review forms and cart modification deadlines, while Donna checks the doubles ladder standings at the Rec Center to see where Pruitt-Kowalski stands. Over at his porch in Hal's House, Hal sits content in the hazy October evening, planning to oil the hinges on his good chair before Saturday's dinner at Rosa's. Rosa, at the Town Square ice cream stand, is taking a quiet moment with a small cone while she sketches out her menu for the weekend.
events: Gary (street bulletin board): Read the board for Architectural Review forms and deadlines for cart modifications
Donna (ladder standings board): Check where Pruitt-Kowalski stands on the doubles ladder

Hal waited: Sitting in the porch chair with the haze rolling in, street's quiet, notebook closed. Thinking I'll oil the hinges on the good chair before Saturday so I'm not squeaking into Rosa's dinner.
Rosa (ice cream stand): Grab a small cone and sit a minute while I sketch Saturday's menu in my head

gary.thought_process: I just got back from signing the cart up at the parade table, noting lights and sound pending review. L-01 says exterior cart mods visible from the street need Architectural Review approval, so I can't just start bolting lights on. Nobody's around at 8 PM, and the street bulletin board is the likeliest place to find the Architectural Review process or a submission form. Quiet hours don't matter yet, but I should check the rules before touching the cart. Reading the board is a useful step toward getting the cart approved before the parade.

parameters.content: Read the board for Architectural Review forms and deadlines for cart modifications

donna.thought_process: I'm alone at the Rec Center at 8:17 PM, no one around. Gary and I signed up 'Pruitt-Kowalski' on the ladder back at tick 83, so the ladder standings board is the natural thing to check. I want to see where we stand, and if anyone else is climbing past us. That's the best use of this hour for my goal of climbing the ladder. After that I can book a court slot at the kiosk for our next practice, keeping to the 2-hour limit under L-05.

parameters.content: Check where Pruitt-Kowalski stands on the doubles ladder

hal.thought_process: Gary's cart and Donna's flamingos are squared away, so the notebook's cleaned up. I've watched this street out of habit for an hour and nobody's out in this haze. Saturday dinner at Rosa's is set, and I've got a chair to haul. Nothing left to file, so I'll stop fidgeting with the notebook, sit tight, and let the evening settle.

parameters.content: Sitting in the porch chair with the haze rolling in, street's quiet, notebook closed. Thinking I'll oil the hinges on the good chair before Saturday so I'm not squeaking into Rosa's dinner.

rosa.thought_process: I'm at the Town Square at 8 PM on a Wednesday and nobody's around. Gary and Donna are both confirmed for Saturday at six, and Donna's bringing lemon bars, so dessert is covered. Hal is the one I haven't pinned down yet, and the table isn't full until he's in. The ice cream stand is the closest thing to a gathering spot here, so I'll treat myself and use the quiet moment to start sketching the menu around the lemon bars and the seating so Hal, Gary and Donna all mix. I can shop tomorrow.

parameters.content: Grab a small cone and sit a minute while I sketch Saturday's menu in my head

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
